paragraphs: When you buy a home or fund a group, you get its board minutes: the official record of what the board decided. Often hundreds of pages.
Checking them for problems is called due diligence.
It uses Reducto, an AI document reader, to turn the pages into data you can check, and DuckDB, a fast database, to spot the patterns.
Next, imagine this on any pile of minutes: a homeowners' association packet before a home closing, city council and school board minutes, nonprofits, or a lender's files.
Every buyer could get a cited due-diligence report in minutes.
